responses.author: simin-yuan
responses.body:
Two data points in case they help with #11494.

1. On the latest release (`@langchain/core` 1.2.18, `@langchain/openai` 1.6.2, `@langchain/langgraph` 1.5.1), `createReactAgent` with `new ChatOpenAI({ streaming: true })` still runs the cut-off call end to end. A `write_file` call cut in the middle of line 17 of a 40-line file writes the first 16 lines plus part of line 17, the tool returns success, and the agent answers "Done.". Same with `useResponsesApi: true`. With `streaming: false` the call is not run.

2. The same happens when the stream ends with no finish reason at all (the body closes cleanly, no `[DONE]`), which is what a proxy or server dropping the stream looks like. The approach in #11494 keys on `finishReason === "length"` in `ChatModelStream`, so it can't catch that case. Also, in the agent runs above the call is built by `collapseToolCallChunks` (`src/messages/utils.ts`, the `parsePartialJson` call at line 634 on current main), which #11494 doesn't change.

Harness and per-run server logs: https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-cutoff-bench

Python has the same behaviour; it is tracked in langchain-ai/langchain#41285.
responses.reviewedClassification: independent current LangChain cutoff benchmark; no PSJ evaluation or adoption reported

responses.author: simin-yuan
responses.body: Opened #11994 for this. It doesn't key on the finish reason, so it also covers a stream that just ends. A correction to my previous comment: #11494 was closed in September without being merged, and #11471 (open since August) keys on `finish_reason === "length"`, so a dropped stream is still uncovered on both.
responses.reviewedClassification: independent native LangChain fix PR 11994; previous PR status corrected; no PSJ evaluation or adoption reported

responses.author: nedonatelli
responses.body: Thanks — this was useful. We traced it through our Anthropic path and you're right on two counts: the max_tokens stop reason arrives after `content_block_stop` and is never checked before dispatch, and a stream that ends without a terminal event currently defaults to `end_turn`. The ML-15 fix will cover both in-tree: carry the truncation reason on the pending call, refuse dispatch when its arguments needed repair, and treat a missing terminal event as incomplete rather than finished. We'll use your test shape as the regression test (a counter tool: one complete call runs once, truncated or interrupted calls run zero times). We won't take an external dependency or run the demo for this; our primary path is native Ollama, which has no message-terminal event comparable to `message_stop`, so a call whose JSON closed on its own is treated as complete there.
responses.reviewedClassification: problem and regression-test-shape validation, not PSJ adoption

responses.author: chiarorosa
responses.body:
I reproduced the duplicate-ID batch in local SDK-response tests and have a proposed fix ready: https://github.com/chiarorosa/typescript-agent/commit/dd315f7

The guard rejects an executable batch before dispatch when two function calls share a `call_id`. Neither callback runs and no follow-up request is sent. It covers the initial response, subsequent turns, and the pending batch after `stopWhen`. Manual-only batches remain unchanged; this does not solve caller-managed result correlation.

The five focused tests pass. Disabling the guard makes the three duplicate-ID regressions fail, while both controls still pass. The full unit suite (1,253 tests), lint, typecheck and build passed. These are simulated responses, not live-provider evidence.

This also changes two existing tests that assumed duplicate IDs would execute. Would rejecting the whole ambiguous batch match the intended behavior, rather than deduplicating it? If so, I can open a PR with the fix, tests and changeset.

responses.author: jagreehal
responses.body:
Thanks for the clear fixture. I reproduced it on main with `streamText` and with `generateText`, since the non-streaming path calls the same mapper.

`length` should win. A truncated turn should never dispatch a tool, and the OpenAI and Anthropic providers report `length` for the same case. Your one-line change is the fix, and #1093 ships it with a regression test. With the patch, your fixture reports `length` and runs the tool zero times. The `stop` control still runs it once.

The fix goes out in the next patch release.

responses.author: nbonamy
responses.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and reproducer. This is fixed in [ead0cca](https://github.com/nbonamy/multi-llm-ts/commit/ead0cca0a45c9f562a5ccdff4b7c8c6f86c34f44) and published in [v5.1.2](https://github.com/nbonamy/multi-llm-ts/releases/tag/v5.1.2), now available on npm.

The Chat Completions adapter now keeps an index-to-call-ID map for each streaming round, so interleaved argument deltas that omit `id` are routed to the correct tool call. It also clones the tool-call data before stripping `index`, preserving the original SDK chunks for other observers.

A regression test covers the reported interleaved sequence, verifies that the two tools receive `{ message: 'alpha' }` and `{ message: 'beta' }`, and checks that the original chunks retain their indexes. The release checks passed.

To upgrade:

```sh
npm install multi-llm-ts@5.1.2
```

responses.author: jaryl
responses.body: Shipped in 0.11.0-next.1 (PR #84, on npm under `@next`): `finishReason` on `ConverseResult`, `model.turn`, `ConversationResult` and `EngineResult`, mapped from Anthropic `stop_reason` and the OpenAI dialect `finish_reason`; a terminal call on a `length` turn is refused and a cut-off prose answer ends with `stopReason: "length"` (`runAgent()` throws `TruncatedAnswerError`).
responses.reviewedClassification: native finishReason/truncation fix published in 0.11.0-next.1; no PSJ run confirmed
